why: A .env stored in Git LFS has a pointer in the index and its real content only in a smudged checkout, which is what the client loads. A .env is not an agent file, so the reader names no reading problem for it, and the pointer text holds no variable: the rule passed with nothing to say. The fail side tracks .gitattributes routing .env through LFS and a pointer in place of .env. The pass side tracks the same .gitattributes and a plain .env with a harmless port. Read the pointer as an ordinary .env and the fail side goes green.
